dedupe_keys.name: dccluster opt open source simulation benchmark for sustainable geo temporal data centre workload scheduling

description: DCcluster-Opt is an open-source, high-fidelity simulation benchmark for sustainable geo-temporal task scheduling across a configurable cluster of data centres. It combines curated real-world datasets, namely AI workload traces, grid carbon intensity, electricity markets and weather for 20 global regions, cloud transmission costs and empirical network delay parameters, with physics-informed models of CPUs, GPUs, memory and HVAC energy and of components such as heat recovery. A top-level agent must reassign or defer tasks that arrive with resource and service-level requirements, and a modular reward system lets users study trade-offs among carbon emissions, energy cost, service levels and water use; a Gymnasium API provides reinforcement learning and rule-based baseline controllers. Producer: Guillen-Perez, Naug, Gundecha, Sarkar and seven co-authors; the abstract page shows one version submitted on 31 October 2025 to NeurIPS 2025. Coverage: 20 global regions. Access: the abstract calls it open source but the repository link was not read here. Licence and cost: not confirmed for the software; the paper is free to read under the arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence. Caveats: results and dataset details come from the paper, and the licences of the bundled datasets were not checked. Simulation uses: it supports optimisation of workload placement against carbon, cost and water, and data centre capacity planning. Related records: the NLR generative AI workload power profiles (data-nlr-genai-workload-power-profiles) and the Google cluster workload traces (data-google-cluster-workload-traces).
